method.name: Mixture of Experts
method.principle: Independent expert lenses interpret the same Outliner evidence; only compatible, evidence-supported contributions are integrated into decisions and execution.

experts.label: Orientation & Control Expert
experts.mission: Resolve primitives, signal identity, and controller validity before acceleration.
assumptions: A schedule cue is intended to select an executable task.
Native eligible task IDs are the valid actuators in the current control surface.
Recorded completion or documented state transition is attributable feedback; missing completion does not prove no attempt.
derivation: Euclidean construction fails when a cue cannot be traced to an eligible task identity.
Unkeyed free text loses routing and attribution information.
A reference-to-actuator gap leaves the portfolio open-loop.
Sparse completion history cannot support SPC limits or causal process claims.
experts.proposal: Reject unidentified cues as control inputs, bind the three designated actions to exact task IDs, run them as a closed-loop WIP-gated pilot, and keep the inferred tax sequence conditional until its dependency is validated.
risks: Completion records omit attempts, elapsed effort, and external blockers.
Taskless projects may be deliberate containers rather than defects.
Task titles do not establish urgency, effort, or deadlines.
experts.falsified_by: Two genuine task-ID-linked review cycles produce no attributable transition and documented blockers, task ambiguity, or missing state recording explain the result better than cue integrity.

experts.label: Decision & Risk Expert
experts.mission: Choose reversible, information-rich bets while protecting downside and uncertainty.
assumptions: The evidence is descriptive rather than causal.
Task names do not establish urgency, difficulty, duration, or consequence.
Probabilities remain unknown until prospective observations exist.
derivation: Zero cue coverage plus low output raises but does not prove the cue-ambiguity hypothesis.
A task-ID scheduling pilot is a reversible process bet with high information value.
Deadline, delay consequence, reversibility, and lead-time facts should dominate semantic urgency guesses.
Every active project needs one explicit next action or an explicit pause, without expanding active WIP.
experts.proposal: Run one risk-and-optionality triage gate, then test task-ID scheduling for seven days while narrowly repairing portfolio executability and keeping outcomes separate from decision quality.
risks: A single completion is not a stable personal base rate.
Zero habit logs may reflect non-use of the record rather than no action.
Tasks may be scheduled elsewhere or blocked by unobserved dependencies.
experts.falsified_by: Explicitly scheduled tasks receive genuine work opportunities but remain unchanged for documented reasons unrelated to cue ambiguity, or fact-finding shows no meaningful deadline, penalty, capacity constraint, or lead time.

experts.label: Execution Systems Expert
experts.mission: Convert validated priorities into a low-WIP critical path with observable artifacts.
assumptions: The current constraint is dispatch from eligible task to task-linked execution cue, not task supply.
Only completion or an explicit external wait releases the next hands-on item.
The tax dependency is inferred from task text and must remain conditional.
derivation: Theory of Constraints locates the bottleneck at release into execution.
Little's Law supports one hands-on item rather than nine competing tasks.
OODA favors shortening decision-to-action latency and learning from each artifact or blocker.
Amdahl's Law justifies early launch only when a real external lead time is confirmed.
Pareto favors one bounded first block over a complete productivity redesign.
experts.proposal: Adopt the three-action sequential recovery queue, maintain one task-ID-linked cue per day, move genuine external waits to a separate lane, and switch to an external-lead-time critical path only when deadline or lead-time evidence is confirmed.
risks: The illustrative 36-week queue-drain calculation is not a forecast because the sample is sparse.
External lead times and deadlines are not currently recorded.
The vague typed task Tiger mode ON lacks an operational definition of done and should not drive the critical path.
experts.falsified_by: An exact task ID, protected block, explicit done condition, and WIP=1 produce no transition within the recovery window, while documented dependency, access, ambiguity, or state-recording problems better explain the result.

integration_gate: Must trace to current Outliner evidence
Must change a decision, sequence, or measurement rule
Must have an observable review gate
Must not require invented tasks or probabilities

syntheses.title: Integrated Control System
syntheses.model: Euclidean Thinking · Information Theory · Control Theory & SPC · Probabilistic Thinking · Thinking in Bets · Theory of Constraints · Little's Law · OODA Loop · Minimax & Margin of Safety
syntheses.problem: The visible cue channel is not connected to the eligible task queue, while recent evidence shows low artifact-producing throughput. Project inventory, executable inventory, and controller state are being represented by different primitives.
syntheses.solution:
### Expert convergence
- **Orientation & Control:** gate every execution cue by native task identity and eligibility.
- **Decision & Risk:** run a brief deadline/consequence/reversibility/lead-time exception gate, then protect the current reversible test until its review gate; do not invent certainty from a non-due outcome.
- **Execution Systems:** run one active task at a time and require each timebox to end in a done artifact or an exact blocker artifact.

### Integrated operating rule
**Identity → eligibility → decision → one-task execution → artifact → review.** Future phases unlock only when the prior gate produces observable evidence.

context_applications.label: Orientation & Control
context_applications.application: Your latest Life OS chooses AR-11, financial-process clarity, and the internet warning, while explicitly placing the lung scan outside this cycle. The current Augmented Intelligence controller instead includes the lung scan, and the financial task sits under retired Housing. This is a real priority conflict: either the health concern intentionally overrides the earlier plan, or the Housing/financial responsibility still needs clarification. The vague “house document paperwork” cue should not silently decide that choice.
context_applications.decision_implication: Start the shared AR-11 priority; before the second slot, explicitly choose whether health overrides the Life OS deferral or whether the Housing/financial responsibility still exists.

context_applications.label: Decision & Risk
context_applications.application: The lung task says you have a “strange feeling,” but the Outliner contains no medical instruction, urgency, or lead time—and Life OS deliberately deferred it. A brief provider contact can test whether there is a concrete reason to override that decision without treating the task wording as medical evidence. AR-11 and the internet warning remain shared priorities across both views.
context_applications.decision_implication: Use professional scheduling or referral information—not unevaluated concern—to decide whether the lung scan should displace the deferred financial responsibility.

context_applications.label: Execution Systems
context_applications.application: Your own operating notes say your current level is one small task a day, that you want to live in the “next hour,” and that the jet stream is about becoming the person whose momentum begins to carry itself. The Life OS review shows 0/3 previous actions completed, so one real closure is not trivial—it is evidence for that identity. A verified task update, appointment, or provider ticket makes “I act” more true without requiring you to manage every project at once.
context_applications.decision_implication: Judge today by one concrete closure in the next hour; let that proof—not the size of the remaining backlog—define progress.

context_decision.choice: Start AR-11 now; before the second slot, personally resolve the lung-versus-Housing priority conflict instead of letting two systems choose differently.
context_decision.why: AR-11 is shared by both plans. The next disagreement is whether to spend the following slot on health scheduling or an unresolved financial/Housing responsibility, so it requires an explicit choice.
context_decision.alternative: Keep the lung scan deferred and clarify whether the retired-Housing financial task still matters unless provider information gives a concrete reason to override.
context_decision.review: After the AR-11 block has a verified next state and after one bounded provider or responsibility check—then retain only the priority you intentionally choose.

context_actions.label: AR-11 form
context_actions.move: Give the next focused block to the AR-11 task. The personal win is replacing an open label with verified progress or one known next requirement.
context_actions.done_when: You have verified progress, one exact next requirement, or a precise blocker.

context_actions.label: Schedule lung-health scan
context_actions.move: Before silently overriding Life OS, contact the provider for scheduling, referral, or lead-time information. Use the answer to decide whether this health concern belongs in the current cycle.
context_actions.done_when: You have an appointment or exact requirement, or enough professional information to keep the task explicitly deferred.

context_actions.label: Internet disruption warning
context_actions.move: Follow the provider’s requested step so the warning has an owner, a response path, and a defined next state.
context_actions.done_when: The warning is cleared or a provider ticket and response window exist.

syntheses.disagreement: The control expert favors the existing 48-hour review gate, the execution expert proposed a 72-hour falsification test, and the decision-risk expert proposed a seven-day task-ID scheduling pilot. The blueprint preserves the 48-hour checkpoint as the earliest decision gate and continues prospective evidence collection through day 7 before making a stronger causal or model-weight update.

syntheses.title: Artifact-First Single Queue
syntheses.model: Theory of Constraints · Little's Law · OODA Loop · Pareto Frontier
syntheses.problem: Task state alone does not reveal whether execution started, stalled, or produced useful intermediate evidence; recent eligible closure throughput is low.
syntheses.solution:
### Model contributions
- **Theory of Constraints:** treat artifact-producing initiation—not project count—as the current constraint.
- **Little's Law:** active WIP stays at one; queued work does not become active work.
- **OODA:** every timebox closes the loop with either a done artifact or a precise blocker.
- **Pareto:** stop when the minimum decision-enabling artifact exists; do not gold-plate.

### Draft solution
Run the three current actions sequentially. A screenshot, ticket, confirmation, or exact requirement counts as loop-closing evidence even when the parent task remains open.

**Decision:** advance only after evidence is saved; external waiting may overlap, active effort may not.

context_applications.label: Theory of Constraints
context_applications.application: Your Outliner already contains plans, frameworks, and meaningful projects. The present constraint is converting intention into a verified external result. Building another system would add planning material without changing an external outcome; advancing the AR-11 task to a verified next state or obtaining a scan decision would.
context_applications.decision_implication: Put your best energy into the point where intention becomes a real-world result, not into expanding the planning layer.

context_applications.label: Little's Law
context_applications.application: Taxes, travel, hair-loss research, health, maintenance, and identity growth represent different parts of your life. Treating all of them as simultaneous current commitments makes no priority choice. Deferring most of them is an explicit allocation decision that gives one selected obligation an uninterrupted block.
context_applications.decision_implication: Select only one current task; deferred projects remain valid without becoming today’s commitments.

context_applications.label: OODA Loop
context_applications.application: A verified task update, appointment, or ticket changes the external situation: a task has a known next state, a health uncertainty has a professional next step, or an infrastructure problem has an owner. Each outcome changes what you can decide next; an unchanged open task plus more analysis does not.
context_applications.decision_implication: Choose the move most likely to leave you with new external evidence before the block ends.

context_applications.label: Pareto Frontier
context_applications.application: You do not need to complete the entire surrounding project to satisfy today’s decision. For now, verified AR-11 progress or one known requirement, a scan appointment or explicit deferral, or an internet ticket is enough. Stop when further work no longer changes the next decision, preserving time for the rest of your life.
context_applications.decision_implication: Define “enough for today” before starting and stop when that evidence exists.

context_decision.choice: Measure today by one documented external outcome.
context_decision.why: One documented outcome proves follow-through; partial progress across several life areas leaves no comparable evidence.
context_decision.alternative: If the first task cannot produce evidence in its block, capture the exact blocker and redesign only its next move.
context_decision.review: At the end of each bounded block; continue only when the next step remains clear and worthwhile.

context_actions.label: AR-11 form
context_actions.move: Aim for verified progress or the one missing requirement—not an assumed completion path.
context_actions.done_when: The task has a verified next state, one exact requirement, or a precise blocker.

context_actions.label: Schedule lung-health scan
context_actions.move: Aim for a calendar date or a professional requirement that tells you what happens next.
context_actions.done_when: The health uncertainty has an appointment or a defined escalation path.

context_actions.label: Internet disruption warning
context_actions.move: Aim for the warning to have an explicit owner, response path, and next state.
context_actions.done_when: The warning is resolved or tied to a provider ticket and response window.

syntheses.title: Identity-Gated Control Plane
syntheses.model: Euclidean Thinking · Information Theory · Control Theory & SPC
syntheses.problem: A populated schedule field currently appears actionable even though its only cue has no task identity and zero eligible-task coverage.
syntheses.solution:
### Model contributions
- **Euclidean:** redefine a valid cue as `native task ID + eligible state + current decision`. Text alone is context.
- **Information Theory:** reject messages that cannot route to a validated queue item; they add occupancy without verified control signal.
- **Control Theory/SPC:** keep the active controller stable until a scheduled review or a genuine exception signal.

### Draft solution
Use an **identity gate** before any cue enters execution. The current Housing-like text remains visible context but cannot override the selected eligible sequence.

**Decision:** ignore unidentified cues for control purposes; review the controller at the explicit gate.

context_applications.label: Euclidean Thinking
context_applications.application: “House document paperwork” is not just vague: it points toward Housing, while the related financial-clarity task sits under a retired Housing project even though Life OS names it in the current chain. The personal question is whether that responsibility still exists. Until you answer it, the cue should not count as a current obligation or displace the clearly named AR-11 and internet tasks.
context_applications.decision_implication: Treat Housing as an explicit ownership decision—restore the responsibility, redefine it elsewhere, or release it—rather than leaving its status undefined.

context_applications.label: Information Theory
context_applications.application: The highest-value missing information is not another paperwork detail; it is whether the retired Housing responsibility is still yours now. Resolving that one question would tell you whether “financial process list, clarity” deserves a future slot or whether the vague cue can be released.
context_applications.decision_implication: After AR-11, resolve the existence of the Housing/financial obligation before spending time organizing it.

context_applications.label: Control Theory / SPC
context_applications.application: You have written that fixed scheduling has not worked and that smaller horizons such as “the next hour” fit you better. Use that operating style for the part that is already clear: AR-11 gets the next bounded block. The Housing-versus-lung conflict waits for one explicit review instead of interrupting the block repeatedly.
context_applications.decision_implication: Use the next hour as your commitment horizon and refuse to renegotiate with unrelated cues until the chosen block ends.

context_decision.choice: Give AR-11 the next hour, then decide whether the retired-Housing financial responsibility still exists and whether the lung concern overrides its Life OS deferral.
context_decision.why: This separates one clear named task from two unresolved priority questions without pretending either question is already solved.
context_decision.alternative: If documented health information creates a real exception, move the lung scan forward; otherwise preserve the Life OS deferral and clarify Housing ownership.
context_decision.review: When the AR-11 block ends and after the bounded Housing-responsibility or provider check.

context_actions.label: AR-11 form
context_actions.move: Make AR-11 the one clear task for the next focused block; the Housing and lung priority questions wait for the explicit review.
context_actions.done_when: The task has verified progress, one exact next requirement, or a precise blocker.

syntheses.title: Reversible Decision Ladder
syntheses.model: Probabilistic Thinking · Thinking in Bets · Bayesian Updating · Minimax & Margin of Safety
syntheses.problem: The evidence does not support precise success probabilities or a psychological cause, but decisions still need bounded next steps and explicit review conditions.
syntheses.solution:
### Model contributions
- **Probabilistic:** keep causal explanations and ungrounded odds unknown.
- **Thinking in Bets:** choose small reversible moves that buy information and preserve future options.
- **Bayesian:** update task architecture from observed artifacts at checkpoints, not from narrative confidence.
- **Minimax / Margin of Safety:** use short timeboxes, safety exceptions, and capacity slack to cap downside.

### Draft solution
Use a decision ladder: **execute the protected controller → inspect evidence → release one conditional queue → reassess.**

**Decision:** do not activate the tax or growth queue until the immediate controller reaches its review gate.

context_applications.label: Probabilistic Thinking
context_applications.application: Your open tasks represent different uncertainties, not one generic backlog. AR-11 is a named task whose requirements and timing are not recorded in the node, the lung scan carries unresolved health uncertainty, internet affects everyday reliability, taxes affect financial administration, the NYC and Niagara trip is a travel opportunity, and hair-loss research is an open research choice. Missing deadlines, lead times, and requirements matter more than invented odds.
context_applications.decision_implication: Compare the consequence of waiting and the value of new information across life areas; state uncertainty explicitly where facts are missing.

context_applications.label: Thinking in Bets
context_applications.application: You can preserve options without committing to every open responsibility at once: inspect the AR-11 task to identify its next requirement; ask the scan provider about availability or referrals; inspect the internet warning; later ask yesmytaxes what is actually required; inspect trip timing and cancellation terms before buying; define one hair-loss decision question before entering broad research. Each move buys clarity while leaving you free to change direction.
context_applications.decision_implication: Take the smallest move that materially changes what you know, and delay irreversible spending or broad commitments until it does.

context_applications.label: Bayesian Updating
context_applications.application: Let reality—not loyalty to the plan—change your priorities. A long scan lead time may elevate health scheduling; a clear AR-11 next step may make immediate progress sensible; a yesmytaxes response may validate or dissolve the assumed tax sequence; favorable cancellation terms may make travel easier to preserve.
context_applications.decision_implication: After every external response, ask what became more important, less important, or no longer necessary.

context_applications.label: Minimax / Margin of Safety
context_applications.application: Your timeboxes prevent one administrative task from consuming the day, while the exception check protects against underreacting to a documented health instruction, deadline, or consequence of delay. Preserving empty capacity is also important: your life should not automatically refill every finished slot with another obligation.
context_applications.decision_implication: Cap the cost of each experiment, preserve recovery space, and override the sequence only for documented high-consequence information.

context_decision.choice: First expose the few facts that could change priority, then make one low-regret move instead of carrying every possibility.
context_decision.why: This protects health and named responsibilities while preserving room for travel, research, and growth rather than allowing administration to consume everything.
context_decision.alternative: Commit earlier only when a deadline, lead time, cancellation rule, or professional instruction makes delay meaningfully worse.
context_decision.review: Whenever a provider, form response, tax contact, or booking condition returns new evidence.

context_actions.label: Clarify and advance AR-11
context_actions.move: Use one bounded attempt to learn whether this can be closed now or which exact requirement remains.
context_actions.done_when: You have verified progress, one exact requirement, or a blocker that changes the decision.

context_actions.label: Clarify the tax obligation
context_actions.move: If you explicitly reactivate Taxes after reviewing the current commitments, ask yesmytaxes what is actually required before treating all three tax tasks as current.
context_actions.done_when: You know whether paperwork is needed and what the next obligation really is.

context_actions.label: Preserve the trip option
context_actions.move: When the growth slot opens, inspect timing, fare, and cancellation conditions before making a purchase.
context_actions.done_when: You can compare the value of the trip with its real cost and reversibility.

context_actions.label: Turn hair-loss research into a decision
context_actions.move: Define the personal decision the research should support—such as whether to compare options, seek professional input, or defer—before searching broadly.
context_actions.done_when: The research has one question, one stopping point, and one intended decision.

syntheses.title: Zero-Gap Administrative Critical Path
syntheses.model: Amdahl's Law · Theory of Constraints · OODA Loop · Control Theory & SPC
syntheses.problem: The tax project contains three task titles that suggest a sequence, but their dependency fields are empty. Treating all three as simultaneously active would hide which dependency, if any, is real.
syntheses.solution:
### Model contributions
- **Amdahl:** if validation confirms a sequential dependency, compress that sequential fraction without assuming it in advance.
- **Theory of Constraints:** expose the next blocking step instead of optimizing unvalidated downstream work.
- **OODA:** use each verified response or requirement to orient the next step.
- **Control Theory:** release this phase only after the prior gate and dependency validation, preserving attributable outcomes.

### Draft solution
Validate whether `talk to yesmytaxes` produces requirements for `submit paperwork`, then whether submission enables `get filed confirmation`. Sequence only the dependencies that are actually confirmed.

**Decision:** keep the tax queue conditional; release it after the 48-hour checkpoint only if its order is validated and no higher-priority safety or official deadline intervenes.

context_applications.label: Amdahl's Law
context_applications.application: The Taxes project lists three tasks—call, paperwork, confirmation—but your Outliner does not establish that all three are current obligations. One conversation may reveal that the later work is smaller, different, delegated, or not yet required. Do not commit to the entire assumed chain in advance.
context_applications.decision_implication: If Taxes is explicitly reactivated, treat the call as the only listed tax task to activate initially, until its response establishes whether another step is required.

context_applications.label: Theory of Constraints
context_applications.application: Tax ownership is currently a decision problem before it is a paperwork problem: the Life OS review says to reactivate, delegate, or remove the yesmytaxes commitment. Until you choose, preparing downstream paperwork risks spending time on an obligation you have not accepted.
context_applications.decision_implication: Make the ownership decision first: personally reactivate the call, delegate it, or consciously remove it from active commitments.

context_applications.label: OODA Loop
context_applications.application: If you reactivate Taxes, the yesmytaxes response should determine your next personal obligation. If paperwork is requested, submit only what is required; if confirmation becomes available after submission, obtain it then. This turns one vague financial cloud into a series of finite decisions.
context_applications.decision_implication: Let each external response decide the next step; do not rehearse or perform later obligations early.

context_applications.label: Control Theory / SPC
context_applications.application: Taxes are currently a non-commitment in your Life OS review. That means all three tasks do not count as today’s obligations. But ownership remains undefined until you choose reactivate, delegate, or remove, so that choice belongs in the planned review.
context_applications.decision_implication: At the review, choose reactivate, delegate, or remove—do not let Taxes remain an undefined background obligation.

context_decision.choice: Do not treat Taxes as one of today’s obligations, but make an explicit ownership decision at the 48-hour review.
context_decision.why: You should not treat three unvalidated tasks as current obligations, but the responsible owner and next step still need to be specified.
context_decision.alternative: Move Taxes earlier only if an official deadline is documented; otherwise delegate or remove the commitment if you do not intend to own it.
context_decision.review: At the 48-hour review, then after each real response or submission artifact.

context_actions.label: Decide and contact yesmytaxes
context_actions.move: If you choose to own the tax process, make the contact as the only active tax step; otherwise delegate or remove it from active commitments outside this read-only system.
context_actions.done_when: You have a response or a clear ownership and contact outcome.

context_actions.label: Submit only required paperwork

context_actions.done_when: The requested material is submitted or reduced to one external blocker.

context_actions.label: Close the tax loop
context_actions.move: Seek confirmation only after submission makes it available; use it to establish that the tax process is complete or externally waiting.
context_actions.done_when: Filed confirmation exists or the responsible party and waiting condition are known.

decisions.rationale: A bounded WIP=1 test creates attributable evidence with limited downside.
decisions.tradeoff: Other eligible work remains queued during the immediate horizon.
decisions.review: Review by 2026-07-27T12:00:00Z or earlier for safety, an official deadline, or explicit priority change.

decisions.label: Release the tax critical path conditionally
decisions.rationale: The three native tax-task titles suggest a possible chain, but dependency fields are empty; validate the order before sequencing and do not let the hypothesis compete with the protected immediate controller.
decisions.tradeoff: Tax progress waits until the first checkpoint unless an official deadline changes priority.
decisions.review: At the 48-hour checkpoint, compare saved artifacts, explicit deadlines, and unresolved safety constraints.

decisions.label: Select one growth queue after administrative review

decisions.tradeoff: Both remain queued until more decision-relevant evidence is available.

blueprint.title: Decision-to-Execution Blueprint
blueprint.objective: Convert validated Outliner priorities into observable artifacts while preserving decision quality, safety, and WIP=1.
blueprint.current_constraint: Artifact-producing initiation under a cue channel that is not identity-linked to eligible tasks.
operating_rules: One active task at a time
Every timebox ends with a done artifact or exact blocker
Unidentified cues are context, not control
Safety, official deadlines, and explicit user priority changes can override sequence

phases.title: Stabilize the control loop
phases.decision: Run a 10-minute exception gate across documented deadline, consequence of delay, reversibility, and external lead time. If no safety, medical, or official-deadline exception is found, protect the current controller and execute its three native tasks sequentially.
phases.gate: By the checkpoint, save at least one done artifact and exact blocker artifacts for every bounded but incomplete step; otherwise preserve unknown causality and redesign the action structure.

phases.title: Release one administrative critical path
phases.decision: If the immediate phase reaches its gate, the tax-task order is validated, and no higher-priority exception exists, sequence only the confirmed Taxes dependencies with zero avoidable gaps.
phases.gate: Advance only when the predecessor produces the information or artifact required by the successor; pause for an exact external blocker rather than opening another active task.

phases.title: Allocate the next growth slot
phases.decision: Choose at most one queued growth task using explicit deadline, reversibility, and opportunity cost; do not activate both by default.

phases.gate: Select one only when its deadline or expected information value is explicitly higher; otherwise keep both queued and collect the missing decision evidence.

checkpoints.question: What verified next state did AR-11 reach? Did provider information justify overriding Life OS’s lung-scan deferral? Does the financial-process task under retired Housing still represent a current responsibility?
checkpoints.decision: Choose the next focused block from those facts: continue AR-11, intentionally move the lung scan forward, or clarify the Housing responsibility; keep the internet warning current until it has an explicit owner, response path, and next state.

checkpoints.question: Was Taxes explicitly reactivated, delegated, or removed? If reactivated, did yesmytaxes establish whether either remaining tax task actually applies?
checkpoints.decision: Continue only the tax step established by a real response; otherwise keep Taxes outside current commitments and preserve capacity for whichever of AR-11, the internet warning, or the lung-versus-Housing question remains unresolved.

checkpoints.question: Which completed move best advanced your “next hour / one small task / jet stream” direction? Are AR-11, the internet warning, the lung-versus-Housing choice, and Taxes clear enough to protect either the NYC and Niagara trip or one bounded hair-loss research decision?
checkpoints.decision: Continue the personal pattern that produced verified progress. Choose at most one of those growth opportunities only if the named responsibilities are bounded and real timing or information value justifies it; otherwise defer both and give the next slot to the unresolved named responsibility with the strongest evidence of consequence from delay.

position.headline: Clear the few uncertainties that restrict your choices, then place one deliberate bet on expansion.
position.summary: Your Outliner shows ambition across identity, health, administration, finances, travel, research, and daily discipline. The immediate challenge is not a shortage of goals; unresolved responsibilities are competing with growth opportunities. The strongest position is to clarify or close the few obligations that can constrain future choices, then direct the attention you recover toward one compounding opportunity.
position.momentum: Your “next hour,” “one small task,” and “jet stream” notes already define a workable rhythm: momentum should begin with one visible result, not a complete life overhaul.
position.tension: Administrative and health uncertainties are sharing attention with travel and self-development opportunities, but the Outliner does not yet contain enough timing or consequence data to rank every item confidently.
position.leverage: A small number of external answers can collapse several branches of uncertainty at once, making later choices faster and more intentional.
position.confidence: Medium — the pattern is clear, while deadlines, lead times, and several ownership decisions remain unknown.

winning_moves.title: Create breathing room with three reality-changing closures
winning_moves.move: Give the next focused blocks to AR-11, the internet warning, and one bounded provider inquiry about the lung-scan path. End each block with a real next state: progress, confirmation, ownership, or a precise blocker.
winning_moves.why_now: These moves replace vague open loops with facts. They protect administrative continuity, everyday reliability, and a health-related choice without pretending that task wording establishes urgency.
unlocks: Less background uncertainty competing for attention
A clearer decision about whether health scheduling belongs in the current cycle
Evidence that your “one small task” rhythm can produce external change
winning_moves.tradeoff: Travel, broad research, and unvalidated tax work remain intentionally deferred during these first blocks.
winning_moves.win_condition: Each task has a verified next state, confirmation, ticket, or exact blocker—and at least one is materially advanced or closed.

winning_moves.title: Turn financial ambiguity into one ownership decision
winning_moves.move: Decide whether the tax responsibility is active, delegated, or outside the current plan. If it is active, contact yesmytaxes first and let the response—not the apparent task order—determine whether paperwork or confirmation work actually follows.
winning_moves.why_now: The current tax tasks look sequential, but native dependencies are empty. One conversation can reveal whether the rest of the chain is real, smaller than assumed, delegated, or unnecessary.
unlocks: A finite financial obligation instead of an undefined background concern
Protection from doing downstream work prematurely
A clean boundary between current responsibilities and archived Housing context
winning_moves.tradeoff: You accept a short clarification cost now to avoid carrying or executing an unverified chain later.
winning_moves.win_condition: Ownership is explicit and only the next obligation established by a real response remains active.

winning_moves.title: Spend the next free slot on one expansion bet
winning_moves.move: After the constraining responsibilities are bounded, choose either the NYC–Niagara opportunity or one decision-focused hair-loss research question. Select by real timing, reversibility, information value, and alignment with the person you are trying to become—not by which open item is loudest.
winning_moves.why_now: A life strategy cannot remain pure obligation management. Once uncertainty is reduced, one protected expansion move converts recovered capacity into experience, knowledge, or identity growth.
unlocks: A visible shift from maintenance toward growth
Preserved optionality because only one bet is activated
A repeatable rule for choosing among future opportunities
winning_moves.tradeoff: Choosing one means consciously leaving the other available but inactive; this is allocation, not failure.
winning_moves.win_condition: One opportunity has a clear decision, bounded commitment, and observable outcome while the other remains intentionally preserved.

hidden_leverage.title: Clarity is currently worth more than additional capacity
hidden_leverage.insight: Several life areas are waiting on one missing fact—requirements, lead time, ownership, or consequence of delay—rather than on a large block of effort.
hidden_leverage.why_it_matters: The highest-return move is often not “work harder” but “ask the question that removes multiple possible futures.” A short answer can eliminate unnecessary work and reorder the board.
hidden_leverage.mechanism: Information gain reduces branching uncertainty; constraint-focused action then concentrates effort only where a real obligation or opportunity survives.
hidden_leverage.falsifier: If the relevant answers arrive but priorities and next actions remain equally ambiguous, missing information was not the dominant leverage point.

hidden_leverage.title: External proof is the bridge from “next hour” to “jet stream”
hidden_leverage.insight: Your chosen identity language already favors small horizons, but momentum becomes self-reinforcing only when those horizons repeatedly end in something that changed outside your head.
hidden_leverage.why_it_matters: A confirmation, ticket, decision, appointment path, or exact blocker is small enough for the next hour and meaningful enough to update what you believe you can reliably move.
hidden_leverage.mechanism: Short feedback loops reduce delay between intention and evidence; repeated attributable wins strengthen the policy of acting before expanding the plan.
hidden_leverage.falsifier: If several protected next-hour blocks produce no external transition and documented blockers explain the pattern, the action structure—not identity or effort—needs redesign.

hidden_leverage.title: Your open life is an option portfolio, not one queue
hidden_leverage.insight: Health, administration, finance, travel, research, and identity growth carry different stakes and different kinds of uncertainty. Treating them as interchangeable tasks hides the reason each deserves attention.
hidden_leverage.why_it_matters: The winning sequence protects downside first, buys information second, and then exercises only the growth option with the strongest current timing and value.
hidden_leverage.mechanism: Reversible decisions preserve future choices while downside-sensitive sequencing prevents one uncertain obligation from consuming the whole portfolio.
hidden_leverage.falsifier: If explicit deadlines or consequences establish one dominant critical path across domains, portfolio-style allocation should yield to that path.

pivot_signals.meaning: One expansion option now has a stronger reason to be exercised.
